adultGuidance: Word endings change what a word means. Say the word, then point to the ending and ask what it does. For -s and -es, ask 'How many?' or 'What does he, she, or it do?' For -ing, act out the action happening now. For -ed, talk about yesterday. Let your child draw the lines and read each word aloud.
description: Read root words with -s, -es, -ed, and -ing, and use each ending to tell whether a word means more than one, happens now, or already happened.
learningFocus: Read words with common inflectional endings and identify their root words (RF.1.3(f), L.1.4(c)).
Tell whether -s or -es means more than one or tells what he, she, or it does.
Match -ing words to actions happening now and -ed words to actions that already happened.
Choose the ending that completes a word correctly in a sentence.
